Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
747 PM EDT Thu Jul 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The latest guidance shows a slight uptick in rain shower chances
a bit farther to the north Friday night.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions are
  expected into the weekend.

- 2) Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below average temperatures and mainly dry
conditions are expected into the weekend. 

Canadian high pressure will build from the upper GL today to 
NE by Fri night. The CAA on N'ly winds will support below 
normal highs in the upper 70s and lower 80s. Humidity will also 
be low, with Tds observed in the 40s today across the northern 
half of the CWA. Tonight will be the coolest for most areas with
calm winds and mostly clear skies. Any rural areas could drop 
into the 50s, while the urban and bayshore remain in the mid 
60s. Would not be surprised if colder valleys dropped into upper
40s. Fri will feature more mid and high level cloud cover.

As the high becomes positioned to the NE, an inverted trough 
will develop along the Appalachian Mountains. This will help 
draw some moisture back nwrd from the stalled frontal zone 
across the SE-US. S/WVs in the NW flow could combine with the 
convergence in the surface trough to produce a few showers at 
times Fri afternoon through Sat night. This rain is most 
probable west of I-81, but a few showers across the srn tier 
can't be ruled out depending on how the stationary front to our 
S buckles. While low temps will start creeping up in response 
to higher Tds, Sat high temps should remain below normal.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

UL troffing will persist through much of next week over the NE 
US. S/WVs will move through the broad NW H5 flow with some 
guidance developing a cut-off low over NE towards the middle of 
next week. Regardless of UL evolution, a return to a summer-like
pattern is favored with a notable increase in PWs/sfc RH. Heat 
builds gradually as well, but nothing near headline levels at 
this time. The increase in heat and moisture will increase 
instability and t-storm chances. Rain chances increase gradually
each day through Tue (when there is some consensus a cdfnt could
approach), but admittedly varies which day is highest between 
guidance. ML guidance highlights Tue as the highest day for SVR 
wx, though low probs exist almost daily.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Little to no wx impacts are expected through Sat as high 
pressure passes by to the north. Winds become E'ly Fri and 
SE'ly Sat but remain light. Could have some low clouds at CHO 
Sat night. 

Low chance of t-storms Sun afternoon with an upper level 
disturbance, with the greatest chance at MRB and CHO.

Prevailing VFR conditions Mon/Tue with any restrictions 
likely confined to diurnal t-storms. Light SE'ly winds Mon become 
SW'ly Mon eve and eventually N of W by Tue.

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain in control of the weather through the
weekend, with E'ly winds Fri and SE'ly Sat and Sun. While there
could be some localized or brief enhancements, SCAs are 
unlikely at this time.

Winds likely become S'ly Mon and possibly into Tue depending on
the timing of the next front. Channeling could enhance winds 
along the bay Mon night. Could have SMWs for any stronger 
storms each afternoon/eve.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Water levels should reach a minimum today in N'ly flow before 
snapping back tonight. Anomalies will rebound within onshore 
flow this weekend, with more sensitive locations potentially 
reaching Action Stage. Annapolis could approach minor flood 
thresholds by Sat night.

&&
